assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Food security
items.clue: Having enough to feed a population.

items.label: Mycoprotein
items.clue: Made from the fungus Fusarium, grown on glucose syrup.

items.label: Sustainable food production
items.clue: Methods of feeding people that can continue into the future.

items.label: Fishing quotas
items.clue: Limits on the size of the catch, used to conserve stocks at a sustainable level.

questions.stem: What is meant by food security?

options.text: Growing a country's food within its borders.
Storing enough food to survive any famine.
Having enough food to feed a population.
Producing food without damaging habitats.

questions.explanation: Food security is having enough food to feed a population, which is exactly what this option states.

questions.stem: A farmer rears animals for meat indoors. Which change would improve the efficiency of food production?

options.text: Give them more space in which to move around.
Keep them in cool, well ventilated buildings.
Feed them a diet that is lower in protein.
Limit movement and control the temperature.

questions.explanation: The efficiency of food production can be improved by restricting energy transfer from food animals to the environment, and this is done by limiting their movement and by controlling the temperature of their surroundings.

questions.stem: Fish stocks in one area of ocean are declining. Which action would help to conserve the stocks at a sustainable level?

options.text: Remove quotas and keep the net size the same.
Use fishing quotas and control the net size.
Use small mesh nets to catch the young fish.
Keep fishing until the stocks begin to fall.

questions.explanation: Control of net size and the introduction of fishing quotas play important roles in conservation of fish stocks at a sustainable level, maintaining stocks at a level where breeding continues.

questions.stem: Mycoprotein is a protein-rich food suitable for vegetarians. How is it produced?

options.text: Bacteria are grown on glucose syrup, in aerobic conditions.
Fusarium is grown on glucose syrup, in anaerobic conditions.
Fusarium is grown on glucose syrup, in aerobic conditions.
Yeast is grown on glucose syrup, in anaerobic conditions.

questions.explanation: The fungus Fusarium is useful for producing mycoprotein. The fungus is grown on glucose syrup, in aerobic conditions, and the biomass is harvested and purified.

questions.stem: A new insect pest spreads into a country and destroys much of its wheat crop. Which biological factor affecting food security does this describe?

options.text: New pests and pathogens that affect farming.
An increasing birth rate in some countries.
Environmental change such as rains failing.
Changing diets in the developed countries.

questions.explanation: An insect pest that has newly spread into the country and reduced the harvest is an example of new pests and pathogens that affect farming, one of the biological factors threatening food security.

questions.stem: Why are some food animals fed high protein foods?

options.text: To increase their rate of growth.
To give them energy for movement.
To keep their surroundings warmer.
To reduce the food that they eat.

questions.explanation: Some animals are fed high protein foods to increase growth, which improves the efficiency of food production.

questions.stem: Golden rice is a genetically modified crop. How can GM crops help to meet the demands of the growing human population?

options.text: By providing medicines inside the food eaten.
By providing more food, not improved nutrition.
By providing food grown from cultured fungi.
By providing more food or improved nutrition.

questions.explanation: GM crops could provide more food or food with an improved nutritional value such as golden rice, which is one biotechnical and agricultural solution to the demands of the growing human population.
